Research / biology

DNA / RNA evolution

Historical reconstruction and molecular evolution through computational phylogenetics

All research↗

Overview

Our DNA/RNA evolution research focuses on understanding the historical processes that have shaped genetic diversity across all domains of life. Using advanced phylogenetic methods, we reconstruct evolutionary relationships and infer the mechanisms driving molecular change.

Questions we explore.

01

Phylogenetic Inference

Developing and applying maximum likelihood and Bayesian methods to reconstruct evolutionary trees from molecular sequence data

02

Molecular Clock Analysis

Estimating divergence times and rates of evolution across different lineages and genomic regions

03

RNA Structure Evolution

Investigating how RNA secondary and tertiary structures evolve under functional constraints

04

Codon Usage Bias

Analyzing selection pressures on synonymous codon usage and their implications for gene expression

05

Ancient DNA

Reconstructing evolutionary histories from degraded genetic material in paleontological and archaeological samples

Methods & perspective.

We employ cutting-edge computational methods including probabilistic models of sequence evolution, coalescent theory, and machine learning approaches to extract evolutionary signals from genomic data. Our work combines theoretical development with practical applications to biological questions.

Research directions

Viral RNA Evolution

Tracking rapid evolutionary changes in RNA viruses to predict emergence of new variants

Deep Time Phylogenomics

Resolving ancient evolutionary relationships using whole-genome data and novel substitution models

Functional Constraint Mapping

Identifying regions of genomes under purifying selection through comparative genomics
